summary: Tested the new country-flag + dial-code phone input across the Vietnam detail page DYE modal (desktop & mobile), homepage DYE modal, and Egypt listing planner, plus backend /api/leads. Backend: 5/5 pytest cases pass (IN +91 synced, US +1 synced, legacy no country_code synced, GET /api/leads 200). Frontend: default +91 with Indian flag; country list opens with search by name/alias/dial-code; US/GB/AE/TH/VN selectable and dial code updates correctly; backdrop + Escape close; +44 7911 123456 paste correctly switches to GB (not Guernsey) and strips to 7911123456; destination header stays 'Vietnam' regardless of country; mobile renders as bottom sheet (bottom-0/inset-x-0/rounded-t-2xl) with no horizontal overflow; homepage DYE modal has new phone field + destination select; Egypt planner (eg-planner-phone-*) uses the same picker, submit button correctly enables only when the phone is valid for the selected country (invalid '123' disables, valid '9876543210' IN and '2025550123' US enable).

ui_bugs.issue: Typing/pasting '919876543210' while India (+91) is selected does NOT strip the leading country code. Observed input value remains '919876543210' and dial code '+91', so phonePayload sends phone='919876543210' + country_code='+91' (double-coded). Expected per spec: input becomes '9876543210'. The '+91 9876543210' / '00919876543210' variants work (handled by parseIntl); only the bare-digits case fails. Root cause in PhoneInput.jsx line 56: stripDoubleCode guards with `isValidPhoneNumber(rest, country) && !isValidPhoneNumber(digits, country)`. For IN, libphonenumber-js considers '919876543210' itself a valid national number (12 digits accepted via the mobile pattern), so the second condition is false and the strip is skipped. Suggested fix: for the bare-digits case strip whenever `digits.length > NATIONAL_MAX && rest is valid`, or simply strip when `rest` is valid regardless of whether the full `digits` also validates. Alternatively parse with country hint and compare parsed.nationalNumber length.

action_items: Fix stripDoubleCode in /app/frontend/src/components/egypt/PhoneInput.jsx so bare-digits '919876543210' with IN selected is reduced to '9876543210' (do not require the typed digits to be invalid before stripping — compare lengths or trust the parsed national number).
critical_code_review_comments: stripDoubleCode's second guard (!isValidPhoneNumber(digits, country)) is too strict for countries whose national metadata also accepts the country-code-prefixed form (India). Prefer length-based or parse-based detection.

server.py kraya_phone uses `+91{digits}` only when country_code is empty AND digits length == 10. If the frontend bug above sends phone='919876543210' with country_code='+91', kraya_phone will produce '+91919876543210' (double-coded). Backend could optionally guard by stripping the dial from the start of phone when they match.

Minor: duplicate planner forms rendered for desktop (eg-planner-*) and mobile (eg-planner-m-*) in the same DOM — two parallel React trees for the same form; both update independently. Not a bug today (CSS hides one) but it doubles state and testid noise.

success_rate.frontend: ~95% (all flows OK except IN bare-digits double-code strip)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The country picker, search, portal rendering, mobile bottom-sheet, +44 paste handling, home + planner reuse, and backend /api/leads all work. The only outstanding frontend issue is the bare-digits double-code strip for India (919876543210 should become 9876543210). After fixing stripDoubleCode, re-test: with IN selected, fill phone with '919876543210' and verify input value becomes '9876543210' and dial stays '+91'. Backend tests live at /app/backend/tests/test_leads_phone.py.
rca of the issue: stripDoubleCode in PhoneInput.jsx only strips the leading dial code when the shorter 'rest' is valid AND the full typed string is NOT valid for the country. libphonenumber-js's isValidPhoneNumber('919876543210','IN') returns true (its IN national pattern also matches the 12-digit country-code-prefixed form), so the second guard blocks the strip. The '+' / '00' paste cases work because they go through parseIntl, not stripDoubleCode. Fix suggestion: drop the `!isValidPhoneNumber(digits, country)` guard, or replace with a length check (e.g., strip when digits.length > rest.length && isValidPhoneNumber(rest,country) && digits starts with national dial).
